note: Dated events in the life of each language. Authored, keyed by exact Glottolog name and resolved by machine. A true flag on an entry means the date is approximate and the card shows it as c.

ukra1253: the Ostromir Gospels, in the Church Slavonic that Ukrainian and Russian both grew out of
the Peresopnytsia Gospel, scripture put into a language close to the spoken one — Ukrainian presidents are sworn in on it
Kotliarevsky's Eneida, the first book written in the living vernacular rather than a bookish register
Shevchenko's Kobzar builds a literary standard out of ordinary speech
the Valuev Circular declares that a separate Ukrainian language 'never existed, does not exist and cannot exist', and bans most printing in it
the Ems Ukaz extends the ban to imports, to the stage and to sheet music
the Kharkiv orthography, agreed by a conference of both Soviet and western Ukrainian scholars; it is abolished five years later
the state language of an independent Ukraine
swed1254: the runic inscriptions begin; Sweden holds more runestones than anywhere else
the Västgötalagen, the oldest text in Swedish, a provincial law code
the Gustav Vasa Bible fixes a written standard and is the reason 1526 is taken as the start of Modern Swedish
the Swedish Academy founded, to 'purity, strength and majesty' of the language
a spelling reform replaces hv- with v- and simplifies the verb
the du-reform: within a few years almost all formal address disappears and everyone is addressed as du
Swedish becomes the principal language of Sweden by statute — it had never been declared one before
roma1327: Neacșu's letter, the oldest surviving text in Romanian, warning of an Ottoman movement; written in Cyrillic
the Palia de la Orăștie, the first Romanian printing of scripture
the Bucharest Bible, the whole scripture in Romanian
the Transylvanian School argues Romanian's Latin descent and begins replacing Slavic vocabulary with Romance
the Latin alphabet replaces Cyrillic officially
Soviet Moldova keeps Cyrillic for the same language; it returns to Latin in 1989
a spelling reform restores â inside words, reversing a communist-era rule
bulg1262: Cyril and Methodius's pupils arrive in Bulgaria after being expelled from Moravia; the Preslav school develops Cyrillic out of Greek uncials
Old Church Slavonic becomes the liturgical language of Slavic Christianity, and carries Cyrillic to Serbia and the Rus
Bulgarian loses almost all its noun cases and grows a definite article stuck to the end of the word — grammatically it moves toward its Balkan neighbours and away from its Slavic relatives
Paisius of Hilendar's history begins the national revival
an independent Bulgaria adopts the language of the eastern dialects
an orthographic reform drops the yat and the big yus
Cyrillic becomes the third official script of the European Union
norw1258: Old Norwegian is written and then goes quiet: the Black Death and union with Denmark leave Danish as the written language for four centuries
independence from Denmark with no written Norwegian to return to
Ivar Aasen publishes a grammar built from dialects he collected on foot, creating Landsmål — the ancestor of Nynorsk
parliament makes the two written forms equal
the Dano-Norwegian standard is reformed toward Norwegian speech, becoming Bokmål
a reform tries to merge the two into one Samnorsk; it is resisted and eventually abandoned in 2002
sout1528: the Miroslav Gospel, in Cyrillic, one of the great manuscripts of the Balkans
the Missale Romanum Glagolitice, the first book printed in Glagolitic
Vuk Karadžić's dictionary and his reformed Cyrillic: one letter per sound, 'write as you speak'
the Vienna Literary Agreement, in which Serb and Croat writers agree on one literary language
the Novi Sad Agreement reaffirms it as a single language with two variants
the state breaks up and so does the name; the same language is now four
dani1285: the larger Jelling stone, called Denmark's birth certificate, in runes
the Code of Jutland, the oldest substantial Danish prose
the Christian III Bible, the first complete Danish scripture
Danish consonants weaken and are swallowed far beyond its neighbours' — the reason Danish is written like Norwegian and does not sound like it
a spelling reform ends the capitalisation of nouns and adds å for aa
slov1269: Bernolák codifies a standard on western Slovak; it does not hold
Ľudovít Štúr replaces it with a central Slovak standard, further from Czech and closer to what most people speak
an official language of Czechoslovakia, in practice subordinate to Czech
the state language of an independent Slovakia
a state language law regulates its use in public life
lith1251: the earliest surviving Lithuanian writing, a handwritten prayer in a book
Mažvydas's Catechism, the first printed Lithuanian book
printing Lithuanian in Latin letters is banned in the Russian Empire; books are printed in Prussia and smuggled by the knygnešiai, the book carriers
the ban is lifted after forty years
the state language of an independent Lithuania
comparative linguists adopt Lithuanian as a control for Indo-European, because it kept case endings, dual number and pitch accent that Sanskrit's other cousins lost
latv1249: the first Latvian book, a Catholic catechism
Glück's Bible translation, which fixes a written standard
the first Latvian Song Festival, which keeps the language in public voice under German and then Russian administration
the modern orthography replaces the old German-based spelling
the state language of an independent Latvia
restored as the state language before independence itself
slov1268: the Freising manuscripts, the oldest text in any Slavic language in Latin letters
Primož Trubar publishes the first printed Slovene book and coins the word Slovenci for its readers
Dalmatin's Bible and Bohorič's grammar in the same year
the gajica alphabet, borrowed from Croatian, replaces the older bohoričica
the state language of an independent Slovenia
mace1250: Krste Misirkov argues in print for a separate Macedonian literary language
codified as the official language of the Macedonian republic within Yugoslavia — the last Slavic language to be standardised
its alphabet fixed, one letter per sound, with ѓ and ќ that no other Cyrillic has
the Prespa Agreement records that the language is called Macedonian
afri1274: written first in Arabic script, in the madrasas of the Cape Malay community, decades before it was written in Latin letters
the Genootskap van Regte Afrikaners founded to promote it as a written language in its own right
replaces Dutch as an official language of South Africa
the Soweto uprising begins against Afrikaans being made the medium of instruction; the language's association with the state costs it dearly
one of eleven official languages of a democratic South Africa
gali1258: Galician-Portuguese is the language of lyric poetry across Iberia; Castilian kings write their songs in it
the Séculos Escuros begin — four centuries in which Galician is spoken everywhere and written almost nowhere
Rosalía de Castro's Cantares gallegos reopens the written language
co-official in Galicia under its Statute of Autonomy
tosk1239: the Formula e pagëzimit, a baptismal formula, the oldest recorded Albanian
Buzuku's Meshari, the first Albanian book
the Congress of Manastir settles on a Latin alphabet, ending decades of competing scripts
the Congress of Orthography fixes a unified standard built on Tosk
occi1239: the first troubadour lyrics; the form and its vocabulary spread to Italy, Catalonia and Germany
the Consistori del Gay Saber founded at Toulouse to regulate the poetry — among the first language academies anywhere
the Ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts requires French in all legal acts, removing Occitan from administration
Frédéric Mistral and the Félibrige begin a literary revival
Mistral takes the Nobel Prize for literature, written in Occitan
Aranese, the Occitan of the Val d'Aran, becomes co-official in Catalonia
bret1244: Old Breton glosses in Latin manuscripts, the earliest record
the Catholicon, a Breton-French-Latin dictionary and the first Breton dictionary printed
La Villemarqué's Barzaz Breiz collects the ballads, and starts a long argument about how much he rewrote
the Symbole: children caught speaking Breton at school are made to wear a token and pass it on to the next offender
a unified orthography agreed under occupation, which taints it for decades
the first Diwan immersion school opens
guja1252: the first Gujarati printing type cut in Bombay
Gandhi writes Hind Swaraj in Gujarati; his autobiography follows in the same language
the Gujarat Vidyapith standardises the spelling
west2354: Old Frisian law texts, the closest recorded relative of Old English
Gysbert Japix begins writing literary Frisian, almost single-handedly reviving it as a written language
permitted as a subject in Dutch schools
Kneppelfreed — a riot over the refusal of Frisian in court — leads to its admission there
recognised for use in the courts of Friesland
cent1972: Ahmad Khani's Mem û Zîn, the Kurdish national epic, written in Kurmanji
Kurdistan, the first Kurdish newspaper, printed in Cairo
Celadet Bedirxan devises the Latin alphabet now used for Kurmanji
Sorani's Arabic-based alphabet is reformed to mark every vowel
Kurdish becomes an official language of Iraq alongside Arabic
nort2641: the Sharafnama, a history of the Kurds, though written in Persian
Celadet Bedirxan's Latin alphabet, published in the journal Hawar
publishing and broadcasting in Kurdish banned in Turkey; the ban is lifted in 1991 and broadcasting permitted from 2002
mara1378: the Dnyaneshwari, a commentary on the Gita, and the beginning of Marathi devotional literature
Modi script comes into administrative use and stays for three centuries
Devanagari replaces Modi entirely; Modi is now read only by archivists
declared a classical language of India
urdu1245: Amir Khusrau writes verse mixing Persian and the speech of Delhi
the Deccan sultanates produce the first substantial literature in the language
Mir and Sauda establish the ghazal in Urdu at Delhi and Lucknow
replaces Persian as the language of the lower courts in British India
the Hindi-Urdu controversy begins: the same speech, two scripts, two claimed identities
the national language of Pakistan, though the first language of a small minority there
assa1263: the Kamarupa inscriptions in an early eastern Indo-Aryan
Sankardeva's Vaishnava writings and his one-act ankiya nat plays, still performed
Bengali is imposed as the language of Assam's courts and schools
Assamese restored, after a campaign led partly by American Baptist missionaries who had printed in it
declared a classical language of India
sinh1246: Brahmi inscriptions in caves, the earliest Sinhala
the graffiti on the Sigiriya mirror wall — verses scratched by visitors, the oldest Sinhala poetry and among the earliest casual writing anywhere
the Sinhala Only Act makes it the sole official language, displacing English and excluding Tamil; the consequences are severe and lasting
Tamil is made an official language alongside it
nepa1254: the Gorkha conquest spreads it across the hills as an administrative language
Bhanubhakta Acharya translates the Ramayana into Nepali, giving it a literary standard
a scheduled language of India, for Darjeeling and Sikkim
oriy1255: Sarala Das's Mahabharata, the first great work in Odia
a campaign argues Odia is not a dialect of Bengali; a colonial commission agrees
Orissa becomes the first Indian province formed on linguistic lines
declared a classical language of India, the sixth
panj1256: Guru Nanak's compositions, later collected in the Guru Granth Sahib
the Adi Granth compiled at Amritsar
Punjab reorganised on linguistic lines after a long agitation
taji1245: the Perso-Arabic script replaced by Latin
Latin replaced by Cyrillic; two script changes in twelve years
made the state language of the Tajik SSR, with a stated intention to return to Perso-Arabic that has not happened
the state language of independent Tajikistan
bela1254: Francysk Skaryna prints the Bible in Prague, among the first printed books in an East Slavic language
the Statutes of Lithuania, written in the Ruthenian chancery language
Branislaw Taraškievič codifies a grammar; the standard is named after him
a Soviet reform moves the orthography toward Russian; both standards remain in use and the choice is political
a referendum makes Russian co-official, and Belarusian recedes from public life
bava1246: Old Bavarian glosses and the Wessobrunn Prayer
Bavarian chancery writing gives way to the emerging High German standard
dialect literature and broadcasting revive, while transmission to children falls
scot1243: Barbour's Brus, the first major poem in Scots
Scots is the language of the Scottish parliament and courts
the union of crowns takes the court to London; printing follows and the written standard is absorbed into English
Burns's Kilmarnock edition, written in Scots by choice
recognised under the European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages
hait1244: the language forms on the plantations of Saint-Domingue out of French and the Gbe languages of West Africa
independence, with French kept as the language of state and Creole spoken by everyone
the first systematic orthography proposed by Ormonde McConnell
the official orthography adopted, phonemic rather than French-based
made co-official with French by the new constitution
luxe1241: the first dictionary of the Luxembourg dialect
a first official orthography, revised in 1975 and 1999
Luxembourgish made a national language of Luxembourg alongside French and German
a law establishes a commissioner and a twenty-year plan for the language
swis1247: Standard German is the written language; Swiss German is not written and is spoken at every level of society
Swiss German broadcasting expands as a deliberate assertion of difference from Germany
text messaging and then social media put Swiss German into writing for the first time at scale, with no agreed spelling
vene1258: Venetian is written in commercial and diplomatic documents across the eastern Mediterranean
as the language of a trading empire it lends words to Greek, Turkish and Arabic — and gives English arsenal, ghetto, lagoon and regatta
Goldoni writes his comedies in Venetian
recognised by the Veneto region; not recognised by the Italian state
sile1253: Silesian written in German-language administrative contexts, with Polish and Czech features
given an ISO code, which is often the first formal recognition a contested language gets
509,000 people declare it as a home language in the Polish census
the Polish parliament votes to recognise it as a regional language; the president vetoes
fiji1242: indentured labour begins from India to Fiji; Awadhi, Bhojpuri and other varieties are carried together
the varieties level into one new language within two generations
a standard orthography proposed in Latin letters
recognised in Fiji's constitution alongside English and Fijian
arag1245: the Glosas Emilianenses, whose Romance may be Aragonese rather than Castilian — the question is argued
Aragonese is the chancery language of the Crown of Aragon
a first modern orthography agreed at Huesca
given legal status in Aragon; the law is largely repealed in 2013
stan1293: Germanic-speaking Angles, Saxons and Jutes cross into Britain; the language they bring has no name yet
Bede finishes his history and reports that Britain holds five languages — English, British, Irish, Pictish and Latin
the only surviving manuscript of Beowulf is copied
the Norman conquest; for the next three hundred years the language of English government is French, and English is written far less
the Statute of Pleading orders court cases argued in English, because French is no longer widely understood
Caxton sets up a printing press at Westminster and has to choose which regional spelling to use; his choices are still in the language
Johnson's Dictionary, 42,773 entries, written by one man in nine years
the Oxford English Dictionary is completed, seventy years after it was begun and forty years late
mand1415: oracle-bone inscriptions at Anyang — the earliest Chinese writing, already fully formed, with no simpler ancestor found
Qin Shi Huang standardises the script across the empire; the writing unifies while the speech does not
Bi Sheng makes movable type from fired clay, four centuries before Gutenberg
a national commission fixes a standard pronunciation, based on Beijing
a first list of simplified characters is issued, then withdrawn
simplified characters promulgated in the mainland; Taiwan and Hong Kong keep the traditional forms, so one language now has two scripts
Hanyu Pinyin adopted — a Latin spelling for teaching and typing, not for replacing the characters
stan1318: the Namara inscription: Arabic, written in Nabataean letters
the Zabad inscription, among the earliest in recognisably Arabic script
the Qur'an is complete; it becomes the reference text for the grammar, the vocabulary and the spelling of the language
the Uthmanic codex fixes one written version
al-Khalil ibn Ahmad devises the vowel and consonant pointing that makes an unpointed abjad unambiguous, and writes the first Arabic dictionary
Sibawayh's Kitab — a complete grammar of Arabic, still studied
the Bulaq press begins printing in Arabic in Egypt
the Academy of the Arabic Language founded in Cairo to coin modern vocabulary
kore1280: the Gwanggaeto stele: Korean history written in Chinese characters, because Korean has no script of its own
Sejong's court completes hangul, designed so that a letter's shape shows how the mouth makes the sound
Hunminjeongeum published — 'the correct sounds for the instruction of the people'; the preface says it exists so that the unlettered can write
hangul banned by King Yeonsangun after it is used to criticise him
hangul becomes the official script of Korea, four and a half centuries after it was invented
Korean-language teaching banned in schools under Japanese rule
Hangul Day made a national holiday
nucl1643: a gold seal given to a ruler in the Japanese islands, inscribed in Chinese — the earliest writing connected with Japan
the Kojiki: Japanese written with Chinese characters used for their sound, a system so ambiguous it took a thousand years to decipher
hiragana and katakana develop out of cursive and abbreviated Chinese characters; women of the court write in hiragana
Murasaki Shikibu writes The Tale of Genji in hiragana
the school system fixes one hiragana sign per syllable, ending centuries of variant forms
post-war reform cuts the kanji taught in schools to 1,850 and regularises spelling to match modern pronunciation
hind1269: the Rigveda is composed in Vedic Sanskrit, an ancestor of this language, and is transmitted by memory for a thousand years
the earliest verse in a language recognisably ancestral to Hindi
Braj and Awadhi carry most literature; the dialect that becomes standard Hindi is not yet the literary one
Udant Martand, the first Hindi newspaper, printed in Calcutta
Bhartendu Harishchandra begins the prose that sets modern Hindi's shape
Hindi in Devanagari made an official language of India, with English kept alongside it 'for fifteen years' — a period repeatedly extended
beng1280: the Charyapada, Buddhist songs in an early form of the language, found in a Nepalese palace library in 1907
Halhed's grammar, the first book printed with Bengali movable type
Fort William College makes Bengali a subject of formal study
Rabindranath Tagore born; he will write in Bengali and translate himself into English
Tagore takes the Nobel Prize — the first for any Asian writer
police fire on students in Dhaka demonstrating for Bengali as a state language of Pakistan; the deaths are commemorated by UNESCO as International Mother Language Day
Bangladesh independent, with Bengali as its state language
mode1248: Linear B tablets record Mycenaean Greek — the earliest Greek, five centuries before the alphabet
Greek adapts the Phoenician abjad and turns unused consonants into vowel letters, producing the first true alphabet
the Septuagint: Hebrew scripture translated into Greek at Alexandria
Constantinople falls; Greek learning disperses westward
the war of independence begins, and with it two centuries of argument over which Greek the state should use
demotic Greek — the spoken language — replaces the archaising katharevousa in schools and government
the polytonic accent system reduced to a single stress mark
hebr1245: the Gezer calendar, among the earliest Hebrew inscriptions
the Siloam tunnel inscription in Jerusalem
Hebrew stops being an everyday spoken language; it continues in prayer, law and letters for seventeen centuries
the Masoretes add vowel points to fix the reading of a consonantal text
Eliezer Ben-Yehuda moves to Jerusalem and raises his son speaking only Hebrew — the first native speaker in around 1,700 years
Hebrew made an official language of Mandatory Palestine
an official language of Israel; the only case of a language with no native speakers becoming a national vernacular again
iris1253: Ogham inscriptions cut along the edges of standing stones — the earliest Irish
Old Irish glosses written between the lines of Latin manuscripts by monks; they are the largest early record of any vernacular in Europe north of the Alps
the first book printed in Irish
the national school system teaches only English; children are punished for speaking Irish
the Famine begins, and falls hardest on the Irish-speaking west
the Gaelic League founded to revive the language
Irish named the first official language of the state
an official language of the European Union
wels1247: Y Gododdin, a poem in early Welsh remembering a battle in what is now Scotland
William Morgan's Bible in Welsh — the single most important reason the language survived, because it gave it a printed standard
a government report blames Welsh for Welsh poverty; the 'Welsh Not' punishes children for speaking it in school
Saunders Lewis's radio lecture 'Tynged yr Iaith' — the fate of the language — starts the campaign that follows
S4C begins broadcasting television in Welsh
the Welsh Language Act gives it equal standing in public life in Wales
Welsh made an official language of Wales
icel1247: settlement of Iceland from Norway; the language carried there changes less over the next thousand years than any of its relatives
the sagas begin to be written down in the vernacular, not Latin
the New Testament printed in Icelandic
the whole Bible; it fixes a written standard that modern readers can still follow
a deliberate policy of coining new words from Icelandic roots rather than borrowing begins — sími for telephone, tölva for computer
independence, with a language close enough to Old Norse that schoolchildren read the sagas unaltered
nucl1301: the Orkhon inscriptions in Mongolia — the earliest Turkic writing, in its own runic script
Turkish begins to be used for court poetry alongside Persian
the first Turkish printing press in the Ottoman Empire
the alphabet reform: Arabic script replaced by Latin in a matter of months, with Atatürk teaching the new letters at a blackboard in public
the Turkish Language Association founded to replace Arabic and Persian vocabulary with Turkic words; the change is large enough that 1920s prose is hard for young readers
russ1263: Cyril and Methodius devise a script for Slavonic; the Cyrillic that bears Cyril's name is the work of his successors
the Ostromir Gospels, the oldest dated East Slavic manuscript
the first printed book in Moscow
Peter the Great's civil script — the letters simplified and several dropped, to look less ecclesiastical and more European
Dahl's dictionary of the living language, 200,000 words collected by one man
the orthographic reform drops four letters, including the hard sign at the end of words
stan1288: the Glosas Emilianenses — Romance words written between the lines of a Latin manuscript to explain it, because Latin is no longer understood
Castilian used for royal documents in place of Latin
Nebrija publishes the first grammar of any modern European language, and tells the queen that language is the instrument of empire
the Real Academia Española founded, with the motto 'it cleans, it fixes, it gives splendour'
the academies of Spain and the Americas begin meeting jointly, so the standard stops being set in Madrid alone
stan1290: the Strasbourg Oaths, sworn in a Romance vernacular and written down because neither side would accept Latin
the Ordinance of Villers-Cotterêts requires French, not Latin, in all legal acts — and by extension not Occitan, Breton or Basque either
the Académie française founded to regulate the language
a revolutionary report finds that most citizens of France do not speak French, and proposes to change that
a spelling reform proposed; three decades later both spellings are still in use
stan1295: the Abrogans, a Latin-German glossary — the oldest German book
Luther's New Testament, written in a German he said he took from the market and the home rather than from chancery clerks
the complete Bible; it pulls a dozen written dialects towards one standard
the Grimm brothers begin their dictionary; it is finished in 1961, 107 years later
the Second Orthographic Conference fixes one spelling for the German states
a spelling reform that takes a decade of argument to settle
ital1282: the Placiti Cassinesi, court testimony recorded in the vernacular
Dante finishes the Commedia in Florentine, having argued in Latin that the vernacular deserved serious writing
the Accademia della Crusca's dictionary, the first of a modern European language
Manzoni rewrites his novel in Florentine to give Italy one written standard
unification; perhaps one in forty people in the new kingdom speaks Italian rather than a regional language
television begins, and does more to spread spoken Italian than a century of schooling
port1283: Portuguese made the language of administration in place of Latin
an orthographic agreement between Portugal, Brazil and five African states, to bring two spellings together
dutc1256: a line written in the margin of a Latin manuscript at Rochester — 'hebban olla vogala' — long treated as the oldest Dutch sentence
the Statenbijbel, a Bible translation that fixes a written standard
the Dutch Language Union founded jointly by the Netherlands and Belgium, so neither sets the standard alone
swah1253: Swahili-speaking trading towns along the East African coast
the oldest surviving Swahili letter, written in Arabic script
the Utendi wa Tambuka, an epic poem in Arabic script
a standard fixed on the Zanzibar dialect, in Latin letters
Tanzania adopts Swahili as a national language, and uses it to teach primary school in an African language rather than English
UNESCO names 7 July World Kiswahili Language Day, the first for an African language
haus1257: Hausa written in ajami, the Arabic script adapted for it
the Sokoto jihad; Hausa verse in ajami spreads widely
boko, a Latin orthography, introduced under colonial rule; the word later comes to mean Western education
the BBC begins broadcasting in Hausa
yoru1245: Ife bronze casting; the language of the people who made it is an ancestor of Yoruba
Samuel Ajayi Crowther, taken as a boy on a slave ship and returned, publishes a Yoruba grammar and vocabulary — the first by a native speaker of any West African language
tone marks standardised in the orthography, without which the writing is ambiguous
Fagunwa's Ogboju Ode, the first novel in Yoruba
amha1245: the Ezana inscriptions at Axum, in Ge'ez — Amharic's older relative and the source of its script
the Royal Songs, the earliest Amharic verse
Ge'ez type cut in Europe; Ethiopic becomes one of the first non-European scripts printed
Amharic named the official language of Ethiopia
four more languages given federal working status alongside it
viet1252: Vietnamese written in chữ Nôm, characters built out of Chinese ones to fit a language Chinese characters do not suit
Alexandre de Rhodes prints a Vietnamese–Portuguese–Latin dictionary in the Latin-based quốc ngữ, devised by Portuguese missionaries
the colonial administration promotes quốc ngữ over the characters
quốc ngữ made the official script; a literacy campaign follows, and chữ Nôm passes out of general use within a generation
thai1261: the Ram Khamhaeng inscription, traditionally the first Thai writing
the first Thai printing press, brought by missionaries
a wartime spelling reform simplifies the alphabet; it is reversed in 1944
cent1989: the oldest dated Khmer inscription — the longest continuous written record of any language in Southeast Asia
under the Khmer Rouge, teachers, writers and printers are killed; the written language loses most of the people who worked in it
tami1289: Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions in caves — the earliest Tamil
the Sangam poems, the oldest surviving literature in any living Indian language
the Tolkappiyam, a grammar of Tamil written in Tamil
the first book printed in an Indian language and script is Tamil
Tamil Nadu formed on linguistic lines after protests
declared a classical language of India
basq1248: the Hand of Irulegi, a bronze plate bearing words that look ancestral to Basque, found in 2021
Bernat Etxepare's poems — the first book printed in Basque
Basque banned in public under Franco; a generation is schooled only in Spanish
euskara batua, a unified written standard, agreed — the language had never had one
co-official in the Basque Autonomous Community; schooling in Basque grows from almost nothing
nava1243: the Navajo return to their homeland after imprisonment at Bosque Redondo
the Franciscans publish a Navajo dictionary and grammar
Navajo code talkers in the Pacific; the language is used as a cipher because so few outsiders know it
Rough Rock, the first school run by a Native community, teaches in Navajo
still the most widely spoken Indigenous language north of Mexico, and still losing child speakers
cher1273: Sequoyah completes a syllabary of 85 signs, having started unable to read any script; Cherokee literacy overtakes that of white settlers nearby within years
the Cherokee Phoenix begins printing in both Cherokee and English
the forced removal west; the press is destroyed
Cherokee added to Unicode-capable phones and computers by the Nation's own translators
maor1246: Polynesian voyagers reach New Zealand; the language they bring is closest to those of the Cook Islands
the first book printed in Maori
the Treaty of Waitangi signed in two versions, Maori and English, which do not say the same thing
the Native Schools Act; English-only teaching follows and children are beaten for speaking Maori
the first kōhanga reo — a language nest where preschoolers hear only Maori, staffed by elders
made an official language of New Zealand
hawa1245: the first printing in Hawaiian; literacy spreads faster than almost anywhere in the world at the time
English made the only language of instruction after the overthrow of the kingdom; Hawaiian is pushed out of schools for most of a century
fewer than fifty children are estimated to speak it
thousands of children now in Hawaiian-medium education
nhen1239: Tupi coastal speech, learned by colonists and missionaries, becomes a general language of the Brazilian interior
spoken far more widely in Amazonia than Portuguese
the Directorate bans the general language in favour of Portuguese
made co-official in São Gabriel da Cachoeira, alongside Portuguese
clas1250: Tenochtitlan founded; Nahuatl is the language of its administration and of a pictorial writing system
Nahuatl written in Latin letters by its own speakers; the Florentine Codex is compiled with Nahua scholars
the crown orders Spanish only; Nahuatl loses its official standing
recognised as a national language of Mexico alongside 67 others
para1311: Montoya's grammar and dictionary of Guaraní
after the Paraguayan War the language survives as the everyday speech of a mostly bilingual country
co-official with Spanish in Paraguay — the only Indigenous language of the Americas with that standing in a national constitution
an official working language of Mercosur
cusc1236: Quechua spread as the administrative language of the Inca state, which kept records on knotted cords rather than in writing
Domingo de Santo Tomás publishes a grammar and dictionary
after the Túpac Amaru rebellion, Quechua is suppressed
made an official language of Peru
a Peruvian congress session opened in Quechua for the first time
tibe1272: a script devised for Tibetan on an Indian model, to translate Buddhist texts
the Sino-Tibetan treaty pillar in Lhasa, inscribed in both languages
a royal decree standardises the translation vocabulary — an early language-planning document
the Kangyur printed from wooden blocks
west2369: Old Persian cuneiform at Behistun, in three languages, which is what let cuneiform be deciphered at all
New Persian written in Arabic script; the language returns to literary use two centuries after the conquest
Ferdowsi completes the Shahnameh, deliberately using Persian words over Arabic ones
Persian is the language of administration from the Balkans to Bengal
English replaces Persian as the official language of British India
stan1306: the Kedukan Bukit inscription in Old Malay, in an Indic script
Jawi, an Arabic script for Malay, comes into use with Islam
a Latin orthography introduced under colonial rule
Malaysia and Indonesia agree a common spelling, so two national standards of one language write it the same way
indo1316: the Youth Pledge names Malay, renamed Indonesian, as the language of a nation that does not yet exist
made the national language at independence — chosen over Javanese, which had far more speakers, because it belonged to no dominant group
